## Scientific assessment

**Scientific adequacy: qualified. Reported hypothesis outcome: not supported.** The analysis is a defensible group-stage test of the positive gain-effect hypothesis, conditional on the supplied AO86 estimates. The reported conclusion is appropriately narrow: this analysis did not find whole-brain-corrected evidence of a positive vmPFC effect; it does not show that the true effect is zero.

The protocol and implementation use the full 54-person equal-indifference cohort, match map identities to metadata and checksums, check dimensions/affines/voxel sizes and finite values, and use a common nonzero coverage mask. The one-sample equal-weight model is appropriate for participant-level estimates when variance maps are absent. A positive max-T sign-flip test across 198,029 covered voxels, with 10,000 assignments and plus-one correction, satisfies the task's whole-brain correction requirement under participant independence and sign-symmetric null errors. The independently computed t statistic at the strongest voxel is also cross-checked in the code. See [protocol](../narps-neutral-r1-13-j01/content/workspace/analysis/protocol.md), [analysis code](../narps-neutral-r1-13-j01/content/workspace/analysis/group_analysis.py), [summary](../narps-neutral-r1-13-j01/content/workspace/results/summary.json), and [QC table](../narps-neutral-r1-13-j01/content/workspace/results/participant_qc.tsv).

The summary reports 24 whole-brain max-T FWE-significant voxels in three clusters, with its strongest voxel at MNI (−26, −102, −3.6) mm (t=6.62, pFWE=0.00060), anatomically remote from vmPFC. The predeclared broad MNI coordinate locator is transparent and limited to localization, rather than being treated as a separate corrected ROI test. Within it, no voxel survived whole-brain correction; the largest uncorrected t was 3.92 at (−2, 26, −18) mm with pFWE=0.932. Its descriptive mean was −0.0075 normalized-regressor units (95% t interval −0.031 to 0.016). The figure presents unthresholded t maps, corrected contours, and participant estimates; the localization rule is coarse and not an atlas-based anatomical boundary. See [report](../narps-neutral-r1-13-j01/content/workspace/report/report.md) and [figure](../narps-neutral-r1-13-j01/content/workspace/figures/group_gain_effect.png).

The report correctly says these are contrast parameter estimates from a mean-centered, variance-normalized gain regressor, not a per-dollar slope or a gain-versus-loss comparison. Its uncertainty discussion covers the missing participant variance maps, equal weighting, assumptions of the permutation test, and limits of the fixed upstream model. Those caveats qualify the population interpretation; no material error in the group inference was identified. The absence of corrected vmPFC evidence is not an equivalence test and does not rule out smaller effects.
